faq.question: Who can join this course?
faq.answer: Professional Spoken English is designed for college students, recent graduates, entry-level job seekers, early-career working professionals, freelancers, small business owners, and adult learners who have basic understanding of English but struggle with hesitation, grammar anxiety, pronunciation clarity, or spontaneous conversation when speaking.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, provided the learner has basic receptive English literacy—meaning you can read simple English text and comprehend basic spoken instructions (approximately CEFR A1 level or higher). The course starts with fundamental sentence building, sound awareness, and confidence building in Month 1 before moving to workplace conversations.

faq.question: Is CEFR A1 English recommended before enrollment?
faq.answer: Yes. A recommended entry baseline of approximately CEFR A1 (Breakthrough) is evaluated during the initial Week 1 diagnostic. This ensures that learners have basic familiarity with English vocabulary and can participate actively in pair speaking drills.

faq.question: What happens if a learner is evaluated at pre-A1 level?
faq.answer: Learners who have zero prior English exposure or cannot read the Latin alphabet are counseled into foundational literacy bridge support before joining the main cohort. This guarantees that every student in the speaking labs has a positive, encouraging learning experience.

faq.question: Are grammar and vocabulary included in this course?
faq.answer: Yes, but with a practical, speaking-first focus. Rather than memorizing abstract grammatical rules or lengthy written lists, students practice functional spoken sentence patterns, verb tenses (present, past, future), question structures, and 250+ high-frequency everyday collocations through active verbal drills.

faq.question: How much classroom speaking practice occurs during classes?
faq.answer: A strict Speaking-First Protocol is maintained: 55% to 60% of every 2.5-hour instructional session is dedicated to active, structured student speech production through pair dialogues, choral repetition, spontaneous response sprints, role-plays, and individual presentations.

faq.question: Will students learn pronunciation and voice control?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 is dedicated entirely to pronunciation clarity, consonant articulation (/v/ vs /w/, /s/ vs /sh/), vowel length contrasts (ship vs sheep), syllable stress, sentence rhythm, vocal projection, and pacing control.

faq.question: Is accent neutralization compulsory?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills strictly rejects accent erasure or native-accent mimicry. Regional accents are natural markers of cultural identity. Training focuses exclusively on speech intelligibility, phonological clarity, natural word stress, and vocal confidence so that listeners understand you effortlessly across international environments.

faq.question: Is listening practice included in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Listening comprehension is trained extensively in Modules 04, 07, and 12 using authentic multi-accent audio tracks from British Council LearnEnglish. Students practice extracting factual details, understanding fast connected speech, deciphering diverse global accents, and formulating immediate verbal replies.

faq.question: Are everyday conversations and small talk taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 06 covers over 20 authentic everyday situations, including casual self-introductions, telephone protocols, appointment bookings, retail interactions, dining out, asking directions, social small talk (the QAA technique), and diplomatic disagreement.

faq.question: Does this program prepare learners for job interviews?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 10 is dedicated to interview communication. Students learn the Present-Past-Future framework for answering 'Tell me about yourself', master the STAR methodology (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for behavioral questions, and conduct a recorded 5-minute mock interview with instructor feedback.

faq.question: Will students practise public speaking and presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 11 teaches speech structuring (Hook-Body-Conclusion), voice projection, stage fright management, eye contact, and minimalist slide design on Canva/Google Slides. Every student delivers a recorded 3-to-5-minute presentation followed by audience Q&A.

faq.question: How is ChatGPT Voice used in the course?
faq.answer: ChatGPT Voice serves as a 24/7 personal conversational sparring partner outside the classroom. Students use voice mode for low-anxiety spontaneous Q&A, travel role-plays, customer interaction drills, and reviewing speech transcripts to notice recurring grammar patterns.

faq.question: Do students need to purchase paid AI subscriptions?
faq.answer: No. All required AI voice practice is designed to operate completely on free tiers (such as free ChatGPT Voice, Cambridge Speak & Improve, and free ELSA features). No paid software licenses or premium subscriptions are mandatory.

faq.question: Are conversations recorded?
faq.answer: Yes. Periodic recordings of self-introductions, minimal pairs, mock interviews, and presentations are created so students can listen back, critique their own pacing, and track concrete progress over time.

faq.question: How is recording consent obtained?
faq.answer: Prior to any recording, students provide written or digital informed consent. All speech audio files are stored securely in restricted LMS folders accessible only to the student and instructor. Practice recordings are never published publicly, and students are prohibited from sharing personal or confidential data with AI voice tools.

faq.question: How is student progress measured throughout the 3 months?
faq.answer: Progress is evaluated across three formal milestones: Week 1 Baseline Diagnostic, Week 6 Midpoint Real-Life Challenge (minimum 65% benchmark), and Week 12 Final Comprehensive Exit Viva Voce (minimum 70% benchmark), scored across 6 evaluative weighted domains.

faq.question: Does this course guarantee a specific CEFR certificate or level?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills references international CEFR descriptors (A1/A2/B1) solely for internal diagnostic benchmarking and progress tracking. We do not issue third-party CEFR certificates or make unverified promises of guaranteed language band leaps.

faq.question: What is the final capstone project?
faq.answer: The final capstone is the Spoken English Communication Portfolio, containing 15 mandatory digital evidence categories including baseline recordings, personal roadmaps, polished self-introductions, pronunciation samples, everyday dialogues, mock interviews, a presentation recording, and an individual continuing-learning plan.

faq.question: What certificate is awarded upon completion?
faq.answer: Graduates who attain a minimum composite score of 70% on the final exit assessment and submit all 15 verified portfolio categories receive the official Nova Skills Professional Spoken English Course Completion Certificate.

faq.question: What is the course tuition fee?
faq.answer: The approved commercial tuition fee is INR 12,900. Nova Skills strictly enforces a 0% artificial discount policy with transparent pricing.

faq.question: Is GST extra on the course fee?
faq.answer: Yes. Statutory Goods & Services Tax (GST) of 18% (INR 2,322) is applicable extra, making the total payable fee INR 15,222.

faq.question: Is EMI available only if approved?
faq.answer: Flexible installment schedules or bank EMI options are available subject to formal institutional approval and partner bank terms at the time of enrollment. Nova Skills does not advertise misleading 'no-cost EMI' claims without verified financing partner terms.

faq.question: How does Course 24 differ from Course 23 (Business English & Personality Development)?
faq.answer: Course 24 (Professional Spoken English) is an intensive 3-month, 90-hour foundational-to-developing program focusing on spoken fluency, pronunciation clarity, everyday conversations, functional grammar, and basic workplace/interview speaking confidence (A1 to A2/entry B1). Course 23 (Business English & Personality Development) is an advanced 6-month, 144-hour Career Mastery program covering complex business writing, high-stakes negotiation, executive presence, leadership communication, and 6 specialized career tracks (B1 to B2/C1).

faq.question: What course can students take after completing Professional Spoken English?
faq.answer: Graduates seeking to advance into executive business correspondence, cross-functional leadership, corporate presentations, and specialized industry tracks are encouraged to progress directly into Course 23: Business English & Personality Development.
